text.p: - Anatoly Chubais, head of President Boris Yeltsin's administration, said in an interview that he earned more then 1.7 billion roubles last year. His comments followed a decision by parliament to discuss allegations that he did not pay his taxes. Chubais denies the accusation.

- The idea that Yeltsin's sickness is slowing down economic reforms worries Russia's leadership as well as the opposition, says the newspaper, referring to the attampts in the State Duma, the lower house of parliament, to remove Yeltsin.

- The State Duma has tried again to oust the president on health grounds. Yeltsin is give convalescence, says the paper, referring to the Duma's decision to delay until next month a vote on the resolution forcing him out of his office.
- Yeltsin's appearence in the Kremlin on Wednesday for "more than 30 minutes" appears to be an attempt to speed up his return to the office in defiance to his doctors orders, says the paper.

- When Alexander Lebed suggested a revision of the possible "scenarios of Russia's development", the impression was that he himself did not understand the meaning of his own words -- so ecletic and chaotic was his report in Bonn in January 15, says the paper.

- Yeltsin's surprise visit to the Kremlin on Wednesday has taken aback his press office and evidently has one goal -- to prove to certain deputies that it was too early to write him off, says the paper.
- The daily carries a front page catoon showing the president holding a huge stick over deputies' heads. "He could have sent tanks instead," comments the paper.
- Every 79th person out of 100,000 people in Moscow is sick with influenza. The last time such an epidemic swept the capital was 25 years ago.
